title: DisaggregatedSet Meets Multi-EPP: Coordinating llm-d at Scale in production
tldr: Mistral runs llm-d in production and contributed two pieces back: DisaggregatedSet, which manages prefill and decode as one unit inside LeaderWorkerSet, and a cross-replica syncer that lets several endpoint pickers share state so routing scales out.

key_points.text: Disaggregated serving splits compute-bound prefill from memory-bound decode for better service on the same GPUs, but it is hard to operate: rollouts can pair incompatible peers and break the prefill/decode ratio.
LeaderWorkerSet treats a multi-pod replica as one unit (if one pod dies, the group dies) and now supports gang scheduling.

DisaggregatedSet, now part of the LeaderWorkerSet project, declares prefill, decode (and encode) roles with topology-aware placement on NVL72 slices, coordinated progressive rollouts that hold the ratio, and per-role autoscaling.
Cross-revision gating: llm-d shifts traffic to a new revision gradually, only once compatible prefill and decode pods exist.
DisaggregatedSet has been a well-lit path since llm-d v1.
By default the EPP is active-passive: failover means downtime (fail closed) or poor routing (fail open), and the only way to grow is vertically.
Several EPPs without coordination drift apart, each seeing only part of the in-flight load.
The cross-replica syncer is a generic set/get interface; a plugin opts in with about 20 lines of Go by giving the state to sync and an aggregate function.
Mistral's Redis syncer runs every 50 ms in the background, so the request hot path never waits on Redis.

numbers.text: Rollouts happen several times a week.
At 300 RPS, three synced EPPs matched the cache hit rate of a single EPP with precise KV-aware routing.
Over 90% of measurements showed zero discrepancy between local and synced state at both 200 and 800 RPS.
One EPP broke down around 700 RPS; three synced EPPs kept serving.

open_gaps.text: Safer scale-up during rollouts is still landing (planned for DisaggregatedSet v1.1).
Redis transaction overhead grows with endpoints; a batched-set contribution is in review.
A peer-to-peer syncer that removes Redis entirely is in progress.

opportunities.text: Implement another cross-replica syncer backend, or help with the peer-to-peer one.
Run active-active EPPs with the Redis syncer and load-test past the ~700 RPS single-EPP limit.
Try DisaggregatedSet for prefill/decode rollouts instead of hand-managing two Deployments.
Explain why an active-passive router caps inference scale, using Mistral's numbers.
